text:
Colorado and Ottawa both arrive 3-1-1 in their last five, but the routes differ. The Avalanche beat Toronto 6-3 on Tuesday, a Maple Leafs team now winless in four, though they're without Josh Manson and Zachary L'Heureux. The Senators lost 3-2 in overtime to Washington, when Cole Hutson won it. Ottawa also has no William Eklund, out with an ankle injury. Since he went down, Tim Stützle has moved beside Cozens and Zetterlund, and Ridly Greig is up to 17:44 a night from 16:00.

Our numbers see little between them. At five on five, Colorado has 53% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and Ottawa 52%. Colorado's results run ahead of its chances, a +20 goal difference on +12.4 expected, so finishing is doing much of the lifting. The special-teams matchup to watch is Colorado's power play (0.78 expected goals a game) against an Ottawa penalty kill that allows 0.80, and the Senators take 4.7 penalties a game.

In net, projected starters Mackenzie Blackwood (+1.0 goals saved above expected this season, +8.0 last) and Linus Ullmark (+8.2 this season, -13.3 last) have traded fortunes. Ullmark has the better year so far, in only eight games.

Nathan MacKinnon has a 38% chance to score and 83% to record a point, and the Toronto Sun ran a piece on why he's "dominating Canadian television." For Ottawa, Stützle (32% to score) is due to cool off in our numbers, as is Drake Batherson (30%).
